# Use cap-table

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Work out who owns what in a startup through its SAFEs, convertible notes and a priced round — each SAFE's and note's conversion price and whether its cap or discount applied, the price per share, the option-pool top-up and who it dilutes, the fully diluted cap table before and after, and founder ownership at other valuations — computed by a script that checks the post-money and the 100 % total.

**Reach for it when** a founder asks "how much of my company will I own after this round", "model our SAFEs converting", "what does this term sheet do to our cap table", "how much have I given away in SAFEs", or "compare a $12M and a $16M pre-money".

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install cap-table                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install cap-table --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install cap-table --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Startup legal pack: [`--pack startup-legal`](../packs/use-the-startup-legal-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/startup-legal/skills/cap-table/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "How much of my company will I own after this Series A?"
- "Model our three SAFEs converting into the seed round"
- "Compare founder dilution at a $12M and a $16M pre-money"
- "How much have we given away in SAFEs so far?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Review this SAFE agreement before I sign it"
- "Build a three-statement financial model for our seed deck"
- "Write the business case for hiring two engineers"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use cap-table".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every figure comes from the computed table,** and the post-money equals price × fully diluted shares.
- **Each SAFE and note shows its conversion price and what set it,** cap or discount.
- **The pool top-up's cost is stated in money,** not only in shares.
- **Every unsaid term is a stated assumption,** with the other reading's figure when it moves the founders by more than half a point.
- **The reply leads with the founders' ownership,** in plain words, with no mention of scripts or files.
- **At most two lawyer lines,** each specific to this round.

- [seed to series a](../../../packs/startup-legal/skills/cap-table/examples/seed-to-series-a.md)

## Use something else when

- Valuing the company: this takes the valuation as given
- Tax on options or shares (83(b) elections, ISOs, EMI schemes): ask a tax adviser
- Liquidation waterfalls on an exit: this models ownership, not who is paid first in a sale
- Drafting the SAFE or the term sheet itself
